seo.title: PDF Poster Maker – Print Large Posters on A4 Sheets Free
seo.desc: Print a PDF page or image as a big poster tiled over A4, Letter, A3 or Legal sheets: 2×2 to 4×4 or by scale, overlap, cut marks and labels.
sections: Print a poster on ordinary paper

Turn one PDF page – or a photo, chart, map or banner – into a large poster using the printer you already have. The page is enlarged and cut into tiles that each fit a sheet of A4, US Letter, A3 or Legal paper. Print the tiles, trim along the cut marks, line them up using the labels (A1, A2, B1…) and tape or glue them together: an A4 design printed 2 × 2 becomes roughly A2, 3 × 3 roughly A1.

steps: Drop the PDF or image; for a multi-page PDF choose the page number.
Pick the poster size in sheets (2 × 2, 3 × 3, 4 × 4…) or a scale percentage.
Choose the paper, orientation and overlap; keep cut marks and labels on.
Download the tiled PDF and print it at 100 % (actual size).

sections: Overlap slightly reduces the final size. With US Letter sheets, 2 × 2 gives about 17 × 22 in and 3 × 3 about 25 × 33 in.

Most home printers cannot print to the very edge of the paper, so each tile repeats a strip of the image – the overlap, 10 mm by default – that you trim off on one side and glue under the neighbouring sheet. Cut marks show exactly where to trim, and each tile is labelled by row letter and column number so you can assemble them in the right order even with 16 sheets on the floor.

list: Print at **Actual size / 100 %**, not *Fit to page*, otherwise the tiles shrink and do not line up.
Turn off borderless printing and duplex.
Use heavier paper (120–160 g/m²) for a poster that hangs flat.
Print a single test tile first to check scaling and colour.

sections: *Auto* picks the sheet orientation that needs the fewest sheets for your poster's shape; force portrait or landscape if you prefer longer tiles. Landscape artwork on portrait tiles can waste paper, which auto avoids.

Enlarging also enlarges pixels. Vector PDFs from Illustrator, Canva, Word or PowerPoint stay sharp at any size. For photos, aim for at least 100–150 pixels per inch at final size: a 3 × 3 A4 poster (about 25 × 35 in) looks good from a distance with a photo of 3,000 × 4,000 pixels or more. Upscale small images first if needed.

steps: Lay the tiles out by their labels: row A at the top, column 1 on the left.
Trim the overlap from the right and bottom edges of each tile along the cut marks, leaving the left and top edges untrimmed.
Overlap each trimmed edge onto its neighbour's untrimmed margin and align the image.
Fix with a glue stick or tape on the back, working row by row.
Optionally mount on foam board or laminate.

sections: Classroom charts and timelines, science-fair boards, wall maps for travel planning, birthday banners, event signage, sewing patterns, architectural plans and kids' colouring posters can all be printed this way without a large-format printer or a trip to a print shop. For a professional print at a shop, export the original instead with [Print-ready PDF](/print-ready-pdf/) to add bleed and crop marks.

The tool opens PDFs from Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice, scanners, phones and design software, including PDF 1.0–2.0 files with forms, annotations and embedded fonts. Files protected with an *open* password must be unlocked first with [Unlock PDF](/unlock-pdf/) (you need the password); files that only have permission restrictions usually open directly. Large documents with hundreds of pages work too – the limit is your device's memory, typically several hundred megabytes on a laptop and around 100 MB on a phone.

There is nothing to install. It runs in Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari on Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS, Android and iOS. On a phone, tap the drop area and pick the file from Files, Google Drive or your e-mail downloads; the result is saved to Downloads or the Files app and can be shared straight to WhatsApp, Gmail or Drive.

list: **"File is encrypted"** – remove the open password with Unlock PDF, then try again.
**The file is a cloud placeholder** – download it fully from OneDrive, iCloud or Drive first.
**A damaged or truncated download** – run it through [Repair PDF](/repair-pdf/).
**Very slow on a phone** – large scanned PDFs need lots of memory; close other tabs or split the file with [Split PDF](/split-pdf/) first.
**The download did not start** – some in-app browsers (Instagram, Facebook) block downloads; open the page in Chrome or Safari.

sections: Combine it with other PDF tools

Most jobs take more than one step, and every Fileopia tool works the same way, so you can chain them without uploading anything. A typical workflow: scan or convert the pages, [merge](/merge-pdf/) them into one file, put them in order with [Organize PDF](/organize-pdf/), make scanned text searchable with OCR, add [page numbers](/add-page-numbers/), and finally [compress](/compress-pdf/) the result for e-mail. Each step downloads a new file and leaves your original untouched, so you can always go back and try different settings. Tip: give each output a clear name such as *contract-signed-compressed.pdf* so you can tell the versions apart later.

Everything happens inside your browser tab with pdf-lib and PDF.js. The PDF is read from your disk into memory, processed there and saved straight back to your device. It is never uploaded, stored or logged, and the tool keeps working offline once the page has loaded – which makes it suitable for contracts, medical records, HR files, bank statements and anything else you would not e-mail to a stranger.

seo.title: Repair PDF – Fix Corrupted & Damaged PDF Files Free
seo.desc: Fix PDFs that won't open or show errors: rebuild the xref and structure, or re-render every readable page. Recovers text where possible. Free.
sections: A PDF that will not open, shows "file is damaged and could not be repaired", has blank pages, or crashes a program is usually not lost. Most corruption affects the file's index or a few objects, while the pages themselves are still inside. Repair PDF tries two strategies and reports what it managed to recover.

steps: Drop the damaged PDF.
Leave Method on Automatic (recommended).
Press Repair.
Read the report and download the repaired PDF.

table: Tries a structural rebuild first, then falls back to re-rendering pages if pages are missing
Re-parses the file tolerantly, rebuilds the cross-reference table and trailer, drops broken objects, rewrites a clean PDF
Draws every page that can still be read and builds a new PDF from them, keeping text where possible, images otherwise
Most robust; some pages may become images

list: **Incomplete download or upload** – the file is truncated, so its end-of-file index is missing.
**E-mail or FTP transfer in text mode** – line endings are altered and byte offsets break.
**Software crashes while saving** – partial writes.
**Faulty USB drives, SD cards or disks** – damaged sectors.
**Buggy generators** – some scanners, web apps and old printers write invalid cross-reference tables.
**Incremental edits gone wrong** – a file saved many times with broken update sections.

sections: A PDF ends with a cross-reference (xref) table that lists the byte position of every object – pages, fonts, images. If a single number is wrong, strict readers such as Adobe Acrobat refuse to open the file even though every page is intact. A tolerant parser scans the whole file for objects instead of trusting the index, then writes a fresh, correct table. That alone fixes most "damaged file" errors.

If part of the file is overwritten with zeros or the download stopped halfway, the missing pages simply are not in the file, and no tool can bring them back. The report tells you how many pages were recovered. Try to get the file again from the original source – re-download it, ask the sender, or check the e-mail server, cloud trash and previous versions in OneDrive, Google Drive or Dropbox.

Repair does not remove passwords. If a protected PDF is damaged, the encryption dictionary may be part of the damage; supply the password to [Unlock PDF](/unlock-pdf/) first if the file still opens there, then repair the unlocked copy.

list: Open the result in two different readers (for example the browser and Acrobat Reader) and page through it.
If pages became images, run [OCR PDF](/ocr-pdf/) to make the text searchable again.
Use [Compress PDF](/compress-pdf/) if the re-rendered file is large.
Keep the repaired copy and the original until you are sure nothing is missing.

sections: Download large PDFs completely before opening, avoid editing a file directly on a USB stick or network share, keep backups, and save as a new file rather than overwriting when an editor warns about errors.

sections: Why read PDFs in the browser?

Desktop PDF software is often large, asks for updates and sign-ins, and opens files with features (scripts, forms, plug-ins) you rarely need. A browser-based reader is sandboxed by the browser's security model, starts instantly and works the same on Windows, macOS, Linux, ChromeOS, Android and iOS. Because Fileopia renders the file locally with Mozilla's PDF.js engine – the same engine behind Firefox's built-in viewer – confidential documents never leave your device.

sections: Use *fit width* so lines fill the screen, then scroll vertically. Pinch-zoom works as usual. Night mode reduces glare at bedtime. Type page numbers and ranges such as 1-3, 8, 10-12 and press *Save selected pages* to get a smaller PDF with just those pages – handy for sending one chapter, a single invoice from a statement or the signature page of a contract. The reader opens standard PDFs from version 1.0 to 2.0, including files with forms, annotations, layers and embedded fonts. Very large scans (hundreds of megabytes) depend on your device's memory; a modern phone comfortably reads files of 50–100 MB. Password-protected PDFs need the password – remove it permanently with [Unlock PDF](/unlock-pdf/) if you are allowed to.

This page is for reading. To change the document use the dedicated tools: [Edit PDF](/edit-pdf/) for text and images, [Sign PDF](/sign-pdf/) to sign, [Fill PDF Form](/fill-pdf-form/) for forms, [Merge PDF](/merge-pdf/) to combine, [Compress PDF](/compress-pdf/) to shrink and [Rotate PDF](/rotate-pdf/) for sideways pages. Opening PDFs from e-mail and cloud storage

On a phone, tap the drop area and choose *Browse* or *Files* to pick a PDF saved from Gmail, Outlook, WhatsApp, Google Drive, iCloud Drive or OneDrive. Cloud files must be downloaded to the device first; files that are still "online only" placeholders cannot be read. On a computer, drag the attachment from your downloads folder onto the page.

Text is rendered with a selectable text layer, so you can copy passages and use your browser's own tools. Zoom up to large sizes for low vision, use night mode to reduce glare, and have pages read aloud with [PDF to Speech](/pdf-to-speech/). Tagged PDFs keep their reading order in the text layer.

Use your browser's normal keys: Page Up/Page Down or the space bar to scroll, Ctrl/Cmd + and − to zoom the whole page, Home and End for the first and last page, and Ctrl/Cmd+F focuses the browser search, while the reader's own search box gives the full hit list.
Bookmark the page or add it to your home screen. Once loaded it also works offline, so you can read downloaded documents on a flight or in an area with poor signal.

sections: Lecture slides, journal articles and e-books are mostly PDFs. Open them here on a library computer or a borrowed laptop without signing in to anything, search for the concepts you are revising, and export the chapter you need for printing. Contracts, invoices, statements, tenders and HR policies often contain personal or commercially sensitive data, and many companies forbid uploading them to online converters. This tool works with HTML files on your device rather than URLs – nothing is fetched from the internet. To convert a page: open it in your browser, press Ctrl/Cmd+S and choose *Webpage, HTML only*, then drop the saved file here. Images referenced from remote servers are not downloaded, which also prevents tracking pixels from loading.

list: Archive blog posts, recipes and articles in a clean, ad-free format.
Convert software-generated HTML reports (test results, analytics, invoices) for e-mail.
Turn exported Markdown or documentation sites into a PDF handbook.
Save HTML e-mails or newsletters as PDF records.
Students saving online reading material for offline annotation.

sections: Text is set with Noto fonts that cover Latin, Cyrillic, Greek, Arabic, Hebrew, Devanagari, Tamil and other Indic scripts, Thai, Chinese, Japanese and Korean, so pages in any language convert without missing characters. The page's charset (normally UTF-8) is respected.

If your application produces HTML reports, keep them semantic – real headings, lists and tables rather than nested divs styled to look like them – and they will convert cleanly. Drop several HTML files at once to get one PDF with a bookmark per page – a handy way to build a handbook from a set of help pages. Add page numbers with [Add Page Numbers](/add-page-numbers/) and reduce size with [Compress PDF](/compress-pdf/).

sections: Combine it with other PDF tools

Each step downloads a new file and leaves your original untouched, so you can always go back and try different settings. Tip: give each output a clear name such as *contract-signed-compressed.pdf* so you can tell the versions apart later.

Everything happens inside your browser tab with pdf-lib and PDF.js. The PDF is read from your disk into memory, processed there and saved straight back to your device. It is never uploaded, stored or logged, and the tool keeps working offline once the page has loaded – which makes it suitable for contracts, medical records, HR files, bank statements and anything else you would not e-mail to a stranger.

Large documents with hundreds of pages work too – the limit is your device's memory, typically several hundred megabytes on a laptop and around 100 MB on a phone.

sections: Scan documents to PDF without an app

Photograph receipts, letters, forms, notes or book pages with your phone and turn them into a flat, clean, professional-looking PDF. The scanner finds the page edges automatically, straightens the perspective so a photo taken at an angle looks like a flatbed scan, whitens the paper and boosts contrast. Drag the corner dots to adjust any page.

sections: Once the four corners are known, the scanner computes a homography – a mathematical mapping from the tilted quadrilateral in your photo to a flat rectangle – and resamples every pixel, so lines of text become straight and parallel. Landscape pages are rotated automatically.

seo.title: Print-Ready PDF – Add Bleed, Crop Marks & Trim Boxes
seo.desc: Make a PDF print-ready for commercial printing: add 3 mm bleed (mirrored or white), crop and registration marks, colour bar, TrimBox/BleedBox.
seo.compareTitle: {tool}: {brand} vs Acrobat Pro, Canva and printer tools
sections: Professional printers print on larger sheets and cut them down to size. Because cutting is never perfectly accurate, artwork that reaches the edge must extend a few millimetres beyond the final size – the *bleed* – and the file must show where to cut. This tool adds bleed, crop (trim) marks, registration targets and a colour bar, sets the PDF's TrimBox, BleedBox and MediaBox correctly and can resize pages to a standard trim size.

steps: Drop the PDF.
Set the bleed (3 mm is the usual requirement) and how to fill it.
Choose crop marks, registration marks and colour bar.
Optionally resize to a trim size, then download.

table: Final size after cutting, e.g. A4 or 85 × 55 mm business card
Extra artwork beyond the trim, usually 3 mm (0.125 in in the US)
Keep text 3–5 mm inside the trim
Short lines outside the page showing where to cut
Patches the press operator uses to check ink density
PDF page boxes telling print software the finished size, bleed area and full sheet

sections: *Extend artwork (mirror edges)* fills the bleed with a mirrored copy of the outer strip of your design, so backgrounds and photos running off the edge continue seamlessly – exactly what printers expect when the original file has no bleed. *White* adds an empty margin – fine for designs with white borders. Always prefer real bleed from your design software when you have it; mirroring is a smart fallback for files created without bleed.

list: Images at 300 dpi at final size.
Fonts embedded (they are in most PDFs from Word, Canva and InDesign).
Important text at least 3–5 mm inside the trim.

Colour: printers often prefer CMYK; RGB PDFs are converted by the print shop and bright colours may shift slightly.
Ask the printer for their spec – some want no marks, only bleed and a TrimBox.

sections: Choosing a trim size scales each page to fit, for example turning a Letter design into A4 or a slide into an A5 flyer. Keep proportions similar to avoid large blank areas.
Designs from Canva, Word or PowerPoint

Office apps cannot add bleed. Export a PDF at the final size, then run it through this tool with mirror bleed. Canva can export with bleed directly via *PDF Print → Crop marks and bleed*; if you did that already, you do not need this tool.

Home and office printers cannot print to the edge, so bleed is mainly for print shops and online printers. For enlargements on home printers use [PDF Poster](/pdf-poster/); for folded booklets use [Create Booklet PDF](/create-booklet-pdf/).

Prepress software such as Acrobat Preflight, Enfocus PitStop and print-shop upload portals read the TrimBox to know the finished size and the BleedBox to know how much extra artwork exists. A file that only has a MediaBox forces the printer to guess, which is how cards end up trimmed off-centre or with white slivers. Setting the boxes correctly lets automated imposition place your pages exactly.

Online printers such as Vistaprint, Moo, Printful or local offset shops each publish a file specification. Most ask for 3 mm (or 1/8 inch) bleed, a PDF with fonts embedded and optionally crop marks offset from the trim so they do not print into the bleed. Large-format and sign printers may want 5–10 mm bleed instead – just set the value accordingly.
